stories.title: Multiplexed detector system precisely counts more than 9,000 photons
stories.desc: Researchers have developed a new approach that can precisely count from zero to more than 9,000 individual photons. The advance opens new possibilities for studying quantum light at large scales and making precise optical measurements.

stories.title: Research advances quantum computing that harnesses speed of light
stories.desc: Quantum computers have the potential to perform calculations more quickly than supercomputers, but they could be even faster and more energy-efficient if they were built with photons as their basic units, called qubits.

stories.title: Zn doping reveals robust two-gap superconductivity in FeSe
stories.desc: Researchers using the Steady High Magnetic Field Facility have found that zinc doping unexpectedly alters the superconducting properties of iron selenide (FeSe) while preserving its two-gap superconducting state.

stories.desc: Researchers at Cornell have developed a laser-cooling technique that could potentially remove a significant bottleneck in the development of larger, faster quantum computers.
